title: Enzyme Regulation Simulator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Biology
description: Compare competitive, noncompetitive, and feedback inhibition through linked enzyme schematics and Michaelis–Menten curves.

learningObjectives: Differentiate competitive, noncompetitive, and feedback inhibition by observing how each mechanism alters Vmax and Km on a Michaelis–Menten curve.
Explain which metabolic context calls for each regulation mode using inhibitor concentration and probe-dot evidence.
prerequisites: Students understand enzyme–substrate complexes and catalytic cycles.
Students can interpret Michaelis–Menten graphs and define Vmax and Km.

keyQuestions: Which inhibition mode changes Km and which changes Vmax?
How does increasing inhibitor concentration shift the probe dot on the curve?
commonMisconceptions: Competitive inhibitors reduce Vmax (they only affect Km).
Feedback inhibition acts at the active site instead of an allosteric site.
assessmentOpportunities: Students justify a metabolic scenario by citing the slider value, probe reading, and info panel summary.
